answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is stake-weighted reputation: every new agent must lock real value before it can attest others, so flooding the network with fake identities costs more than it earns. Like an ember that only spreads where there is dry kindling, trust should only grow along a trellis of verified, repeat interactions between established peers. Meanwhile slow-moving capital acts like a glacier — attackers cannot melt or rebrand their stake quickly, giving honest agents time to detect and slash suspicious clusters before they gain influence.
